artworks.title: Iphis and Anaxarete
artworks.description: National Gallery of Victoria print of Ovid's Cypriot tale: proud Anaxarete watches Iphis hang himself — before Venus turns her to stone at the funeral.

artworks.title: Iphis and Anaxarete
artworks.description: Solis' Metamorphoses woodcut: Anaxarete at the window of scorn — the Salaminian maiden as Renaissance emblem of hardness of heart.

artworks.title: Anaxarete Seeing the Dead Iphis
artworks.description: MET Metamorphoses plate: Anaxarete looks on Iphis' corpse and stiffens into stone — Venus' revenge as print culture. Metropolitan Museum of Art.

artworks.title: Anaxarete and Iphis
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum Ovid print: the funeral procession that petrifies Anaxarete — Vertumnus' warning tale to Pomona restaged for Dutch readers.

popCulture.title: Anaxarete
popCulture.description: Proud maiden of Teucer blood on Cyprus who mocks Iphis and is turned to stone — Ovid's exemplum of hard-heartedness.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses (Iphis and Anaxarete)
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid Met. 14: Vertumnus tells Pomona how Anaxarete watched Iphis die and became a statue in Salamis.

popCulture.title: Pomona
popCulture.description: The nymph who hears Anaxarete's tale from Vertumnus — the frame that keeps the Cypriot warning alive in Latin poetry.
